lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Ask the server what, which, how, where and how much about dishes, wine and the restaurant.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Ask the server what they recommend, how a dish is prepared, and how much a bottle of wine costs.
lessons.title: Ask About the Menu
lessons.objective: Ask what is recommended, which dish is local, how fish is prepared, where facilities are, and how much wine costs.
lessons.focus: なに asks “what”; どれ asks “which one.” どこ, いつ, どう, どうして, and いくら ask place, time, method, reason, and price. か closes a polite yes/no question, while these question words can appear inside a polite information question.
lessons.scene: Sam asks the server about a regional dish, grilled fish, the restrooms, and a bottle price.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Say not yet, nothing more, another one, more or less while ordering and finishing dinner.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Tell the server you are not ready yet, then ask for another drink and say you want nothing more after dessert.
lessons.title: Not Yet, Another, and Nothing More
lessons.objective: Say you are not ready yet, order another drink, request less spice, and finish the meal without ordering anything more.
lessons.focus: まだ…ません says “not yet”; もう一杯 means one more glass. これ以上は…ません means no more than this; 何も…ません means nothing in a negative sentence. ぜんぜん飲みません states a firm “never” in the drinking context without copying Spanish no/nunca word order.
lessons.scene: Sam delays ordering, requests another nonalcoholic drink, and finishes after dessert.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Ask the server politely for the check, a photo and items at the table.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Ask the server politely for a glass of water and the check, and ask if you can pay by card.
lessons.title: Polite Table Requests and Payment
lessons.objective: Ask politely for a glass of water, the bill, and a photo, and ask whether card payment is accepted.
lessons.focus: 〜をお願いします is a polite request for an item. 〜ていただけますか asks a person to do something, as in 写真を撮っていただけますか. 〜てもいいですか asks permission, as in カードで払ってもいいですか. These forms replace Spanish usted commands.
lessons.scene: Sam asks a server for table items, a group photo, and the bill.

lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Spot dinner cognates and use survival phrases to get help when you don't understand.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Tell the server you don't understand, ask them to repeat more slowly, and ask how to say a dish in Spanish.
lessons.title: Recognize Loanwords and Ask for Help
lessons.objective: Recognize familiar dinner loanwords, state a peanut allergy directly, and ask for a slower repeat or the Japanese name of a dish.
lessons.focus: レストラン, チョコレート, and オプション are katakana loanwords that may be recognizable from context; Japanese has no Spanish -ción/-dad cognate rule. わかりません says you do not understand; もう一度ゆっくりお願いします asks for a slower repeat. ピーナッツアレルギーがあります states the allergy directly.
lessons.scene: At dinner, Sam asks the server to repeat a dish name and checks an ingredient after stating a peanut allergy.
